headline: FRESH reports higher tool-task completion with failure-aware graph memory
summary: A September 2026 preprint proposes FRESH, which stores successful actions, failures, preconditions and repairs in a typed experience graph, then retrieves compact guidance for a frozen language-model executor. On tau-bench, its authors report the highest average pass performance among compared memory methods for three backbones, with average relative gains over no-memory baselines of 10.8% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 38.9% for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and 53.2% for Qwen3-8B. On AppWorld, it reports pass rates of 0.268 vs 0.250 on Test-N and 0.146 vs 0.115 on Test-C versus the strongest listed baseline. The absolute AppWorld rates remain low; all results are author-reported benchmark outcomes and were not independently reproduced.
